doc.title: Leslie Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Interviewing musicians while alive; Grove citations
summary: Johnson says she interviews musicians before they die, and relatives contact her after articles and Grove Dictionary references.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Do you have — I know that major newspapers often times have obituaries ready.
I’m glad. It’s like I know they sort of have to.

No, I know, it’s kind of morbid. No we don’t. But I have enough material on them where — what I try and do is interview them before they die. Because for one thing they get so many letters and phone calls from people once we’ve run the article that it’s such a boon to these older musicians to have the article published while they’re alive. And sometimes it’s such a race against the clock. But I can’t tell you how many musicians have said, “I’ve heard from nephews that I haven’t known anything that they were even around.” Or I’ve had family members call up and say I heard that you did an article on my uncle or

on my grandfather or on this old college friend, can you give me his address. And then they’re in contact. In fact in the Grove Dictionary of Jazz The Rag is used as a reference for a lot of the biographies. And I will hear from somebody who’s read about their grandfather or father or uncle or aunt or — in the Grove Dictionary and then they see that there’s a reference to an article and they’ll call and they’ll say do you have that back issue available, which I may or may not have.

Well somebody has it. I do have maybe one or two copies of some of the early issues and more copies — and once I found out that people saved them or that new subscribers would order back issues like you can’t believe, then I would have a press overrun so that I could sell these back issues. So very often I can provide it. But they’ll say, “I didn’t know anything except that my grandfather was a musician and reading that little bio, now I know something about him and you ran a long article on him.”
Yeah. It is very rewarding to be able to do that.
